_: Every libviprs difference from causl's import-run.mjs, expressed here rather
than edited into the importer. K2.3 (#76) owns tools/contract/config.json for
the dashboard, the era axes and the series palette; when that lands these keys
move into it and --config's default follows. Nothing here is a threshold: a
tolerance is fitted from repeat sweeps by the gate and read from a baseline,
never written down as a constant.
_publishableProfiles: `ci` proves the harness runs and is never a measurement: three reps, a cut-down
cell list, and an archive entry indistinguishable from a calibrated sweep. It is
the one profile that is refused here rather than at the archive door, because
the archive is allowed to hold it and the page is not.

_sourceSuffix: The source image is folded into the series id rather than left as a facet, so
gradient and noise never share a chart line. They are different inputs and one
line through both is one line through two experiments.

_ungateableMetrics: Named here as a floor, not as the answer. The calibration decides what is
gateable per cell; these two are ungateable on this suite whatever it says,
because the free replicate pair already moved p99 by 74.5% on an idle host.
A metric no calibration has fitted is `gated: false` and gets no verdict chip.

_filesystemDependent: allocated_bytes is the filesystem's answer to the same bytes, so it moves with
the block size and is compared only between runs on the same fsType and mount
source. Putting it in the exact list would refuse an honest run on another disk.
_commitKeys: Both trees, because the harness generates the source image: a harness-only
change can move output_bytes honestly and refusing it would block publication
with no way to clear it. The cost is that a harness-only change does not get
the within-commit check, which the gate's own invariant comparison still does.

_anyFailedCell: causl refuses a run with any failed cell because a failed cell there means a
runner crashed. In this family `failed` is the honest label for a scenario that
does not apply to a backend: a directory tree has no root directory to decode.
The run-level form of causl's check is kept instead, and it is `noOkCells`.
